subject: Request for short-term throughput carveout / burst window — Cardinal Health migration
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Cardinal Health Platform Ops <platform-ops@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:22:00-05:00
Subject: Short-term request: throughput carveout for Nov 20 migration

Hi Ava / Marissa,

We're doing a critical data ingestion and model-retrain run during a maintenance window on Nov 20 (approx 02:00–10:00 UTC). The migration will generate a spike in inference traffic as we validate millions of historical records against your embeddings+rerank pipeline. Our preliminary numbers indicate a sustained elevated QPS for roughly a 6–8 hour window.

We need Redwood to confirm a short-term increase to our burst allowance (we're currently hitting fairness throttles) and a temporary relaxation of the request-based rate caps for that window. Specifically: 
- Target sustained QPS: ~350–450 (peak bursts up to ~1,000 qps for <5 min)
- Estimated tokens/hour: ~1.1–1.5M tokens/hour
- Window requested: Nov 20 02:00–10:00 UTC (8 hours)

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a carveout (temporary SLA/ratecap exception) and what the commercial/operational prerequisites are? We can sign an MOU and provide collectors for detailed telemetry if needed.

Tom Hayes from our infra team is on the thread for technical coordination.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Platform Integrations, Cardinal Health
elena.ruiz@cardinalhealth.com
+1 (617) 555-0124


-----Original Attachment: cardinal_throughput_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Short-term request: throughput carveout for Nov 20 migration

Elena — thanks for the heads up. We can support a short-term burst window but need to line up a few items to make this low risk for both sides. Looping in Rishi (solutions) and David (SRE). Marissa — please track commercial terms.

To move fast, please confirm the following by EOD 2026-11-19 so we can lock infra changes:
1) Final expected sustained QPS and peak burst profile (per-minute).
2) Avg tokens per request and any long-tail larger requests.
3) Whether you can route traffic to a fixed hostname/route for the window (helps isolate traffic).
4) Agreement to telemetry and debug logs for the window (we'll enable enhanced traces).

Operational note: our recommended approach is a time-boxed rate-policy override that routes to a temporary dedicated capacity slice for Cardinal. We will enable strict fallback rules (model variant with lower cost + higher latency) if we detect cross-tenant stability risk. We'll require a signed MOU outlining the exception window and extra usage fee. Draft attached (redwood_mou-draft.pdf).

Rishi / David — quick ask: can you confirm whether a dedicated slice + ephemeral rate profile can sustain 450 qps sustained and the tradeoffs on p95 latency? If not, what cap would you be comfortable supporting?

Ava Chen
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com


Attachment: redwood_mou-draft.pdf (PDF, 82KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:48:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Short-term request: throughput carveout for Nov 20 migration

Short technical readout below. TL;DR — we can support an 8-hour ephemeral carveout with conditions.

Assumptions based on Elena's numbers: 350–450 sustained QPS, 1.1–1.5M tokens/hour. To keep latency within a reasonable p95 we recommend: 
- Route traffic to a temporary dedicated pool with pre-warmed KV cache (we'll seed based on sample inputs you provide).
- Hardened prefix/KV caching to reduce per-request compute.
- Limit peak microbursts to 1,000 qps for no more than 3 minutes; sustained above 600 qps will degrade p95 latency to ~650–900ms depending on token length and model.
- If latency or error rate crosses thresholds we'll automatically failover to a lower-cost model variant (adds ~200–400ms p95 but keeps throughput).

Operational proposal:
- Approved window: Nov 20 02:00–10:00 UTC (8 hours)
- Provisioned cap for window: 450 sustained qps; 1,000 qps short bursts (<= 3 min)
- Telemetry: detailed token-level and request traces; we require Cardinal to retain traces and provide immediate access if we need to debug.
- MOU: must be signed by Nov 19 17:00 UTC to finalize infra changes.
- Cost: provisional one-time uplift for reserved capacity + overage billing (Marissa, see comments).

I'll attach a brief plan (sheets) with config parameters and fallback thresholds. Please review and confirm.

— Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardinalhealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:15:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Short-term request: throughput carveout for Nov 20 migration

Elena — glad we're able to move quickly. Commercials in brief: 
- One-time reserved-capacity fee: USD 12,500 (covers the dedicated slice and pre-warm).
- Estimated variable overage: billed at standard per-token uplift for the window if usage exceeds the provisional cap.
- MOU will include acceptance criteria and a liability carveout while the ephemeral policy is in effect.

I'll run this with RevOps for sign-off; contingent on the signed MOU by Nov 19 17:00 UTC we can commit to the window. If Cardinal prefers, I can prepare a DocuSign with the MOU redlines.

Charge code for internal tracking: CH-834 (please include in the MOU).

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cardinalhealth.com>, Tom Hayes <t.hayes@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:00:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Short-term request: throughput carveout for Nov 20 migration — next steps

Thanks all — summary and next steps below: 

What Redwood will provide (conditional):
- Temporary rate policy override and dedicated capacity slice for Cardinal Health for Nov 20 02:00–10:00 UTC.
- Provisioned cap: 450 sustained qps; 1,000 qps short bursts (<=3 minutes).
- Enhanced telemetry and enhanced tracing enabled for the window.
- Automatic fallback to a lower-latency-tolerant model variant if stability thresholds are hit.

Conditions (must be met by Nov 19 17:00 UTC):
1) Signed MOU (attached link) accepting the one-time fee and operational terms.
2) Cardinal provides sample request payloads and expected prefix lists for cache warmup.
3) Primary contact for the window (on-call during the 8-hour period).

Commercials: one-time reserved-capacity fee USD 12,500 + standard overage if cap exceeded. Marissa will prepare DocuSign.

Elena / Tom — can you confirm by EOD tomorrow that Cardinal will sign the MOU and supply the sample payloads? If yes, we'll start infra provisioning today and schedule a short runbook + rollback call for Nov 19 18:00 UTC.

Ava Chen
